newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares rise after GDR surge.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares rise after GDR surge.

text.p: Solidere A and B shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Wednesday following a dramatic surge by the company's Global Depositary Receipts on the London Stock Exchange.
The A shares, which are the underlying shares to the GDRs, rose to $10.5 from $10.375 and the B shares also climbed to $10.875 from $10.75.
The rise in the A shares was their second successive increase this week and followed weeks of stagnation since April 2 during which the shares remained at $10.25.
Both the A and B shares had hovered near their historic lows for weeks before the latest movement sparked by the sudden climb of Solidere's GDRs in London.
The GDRs, issued last November at $11.5, soared on Tuesday to $17.625 from last week's $12. They opened in London at $17 on Wednesday.
Company officials and a British investment banker told Reuters purchases of the GDRs by U.S. and European emerging market fund managers were responsible for the increase.
The purchases followed visits by groups of fund managers to Beirut to inspect progress on Solidere's 25-year programme to rebuild the Beirut city centre.

Angus Blair, a director of ING Barings who brought the latest group of nine fund managers last week, said they were impressed by Lebanon's progress in rebuilding its capital and its financial markets.
